claims.text: The golden CoT method increases the solution rate on a benchmark of detection puzzles with GPT-4 from 38% using standard CoT to 83%.
In few-shot evaluation settings on InstructEval, omitting prompts or using generic task-agnostic prompts outperforms complex instruction selection methods.
In zero-shot settings, expert-written task-specific prompts significantly boost language model performance compared to automated prompt generation.
The skeleton-of-thought prompting method achieves generation speedups close to twice the original evaluation speed.
Decomposed prompting (DECOMP) achieves better length generalization than Chain-of-Thought prompting on list reversal tasks by recursively decomposing input sequences into smaller sublists.

evidence.description: According to a benchmark composed of a set of detection puzzles, the 38% solution rate of the standard CoT approach with GPT-4 can be improved to an 83% solution rate when the golden CoT method is used.

InstructEval benchmark evaluation concluded that in few-shot settings, omitting prompts or using generic task-agnostic prompts tends to outperform the other methods, with prompts having little impact on performance.

InstructEval results showed that in zero-shot settings, expert-written task-specific prompts could significantly boost the achieved performance, whereas automated prompts failed to outperform simple baselines.
Ning et al. reported that their skeleton of thought method achieved a significant speedup, often close to twice the original evaluation speed, depending on the model.

In list reversal, DECOMP exhibits better length generalization than CoT prompting by recursively decomposing the task into the reversal of smaller sublists, achieving higher accuracy for longer input sequences.

methodologies.name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
methodologies.description: A technique that prompts large language models to generate intermediate logical reasoning steps prior to giving a final answer.
conditions: Zero-shot setting with explicit step-by-step instructions
Few-shot setting with manual exemplars containing questions and rationale chains

methodologies.name: Decomposed Prompting (DECOMP)
methodologies.description: A modular framework that decomposes complex queries into structured prompting programs handled by specialized subtask handlers.

methodologies.name: Multimodal Prompt Learning (MaPLe)
methodologies.description: A technique that explicitly couples and jointly optimizes vision and language prompt vectors hierarchically across transformer layers in vision-language models.
conditions: Frozen CLIP base architecture with learned prompt vectors

limitations.text: The scope of the survey is primarily focused on text and vision modalities because the majority of accessible model APIs remain limited to these domains.
Golden CoT requires ground-truth reasoning chains directly inside the prompt, which severely restricts its practical utility for novel problem solving.
Static role prompting suffers from catastrophic forgetting and inter-domain confusion when applied to multi-domain tasks.
Current prompting methods rely heavily on surface pattern recognition and distributional correlations rather than genuine semantic comprehension.

future_work.text: Investigate internal neural architecture mechanisms and parameter distributions using interpretability techniques like activation patching to design structurally informed prompts.
Develop evaluation frameworks and benchmarks that test for genuine semantic understanding and logical consistency rather than surface pattern matching.
Establish standardized benchmarks and community-driven security frameworks to evaluate LLM resilience against evolving inference-phase and training-phase adversarial attacks.
